seo.title: HTWind | Windows Desktop Widget Host
seo.description: HTWind is an open-source Windows desktop widget host for HTML widgets, manifest packages, native host APIs, and controlled PowerShell tooling.
seo.openGraphDescription: Build a cleaner Windows desktop with HTML widgets, native host APIs for system metrics, audio, and media, and per-widget PowerShell permissions.

featureCards.title: HTML Widgets on Desktop
featureCards.description: Build desktop widgets with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. The built-in editor opens multi-file packages in tabs with live preview (hot reload) and a runtime console for errors and logs.

featureCards.title: PowerShell Integration
featureCards.description: Run PowerShell through an in-process engine after an explicit per-widget grant (read-only, full, or deny). Read-only mode runs in a constrained sandbox, and every call is isolated and time-limited.

featureCards.title: Windows Native Feel
featureCards.description: Tray behavior, pin-on-top or desktop-layer pinning, magnetic window snapping, per-widget opacity and zoom, workspace profiles, and display-aware suppression keep widgets feeling native to Windows.

faqItems.question: What is HTWind used for?
faqItems.answer: HTWind manages and displays HTML-based desktop widgets on Windows, making it easier to keep diagnostics, shortcuts, and useful system context visible while you work.

faqItems.question: Can I build my own widgets?
faqItems.answer: Yes. You can create custom widgets with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, then package them as a single file, an asset-backed folder, or a manifest package with one or many widgets.

faqItems.question: What is htwind.widget.json used for?
faqItems.answer: htwind.widget.json is the widget package manifest. It defines package metadata and one or more widgets, including each widget's relative folder, entry HTML file, and declared assets.

faqItems.question: Does HTWind support PowerShell automation?
faqItems.answer: Yes. Widgets can run PowerShell through the in-process engine, and each widget needs an explicit per-widget grant first: read-only (sandboxed), full access, or deny. The choice is remembered per widget.

faqItems.question: Which native host APIs are available to widgets?
faqItems.answer: Widgets can call system.metrics (CPU, memory, disks, network, battery), audio.visualizer (real-time audio FFT), media.session (now-playing info and transport controls), storage.get/set (persistent per-widget settings), and theme.get/onChanged (live theme and accent colors) — all without spawning any processes.

faqItems.question: Can widgets auto-hide while I use fullscreen or maximized apps?
faqItems.answer: Yes. In Settings, you can enable fullscreen suppression and a separate maximized-app suppression mode. Both work per display: widget windows are hidden and suspended instantly, keep their state, and are restored automatically without changing saved visibility state.

faqItems.question: Can I save different widget layouts?
faqItems.answer: Yes. Workspace profiles save the current widget setup — visibility, positions, sizes, lock and pin modes, opacity, and zoom — as a named layout you can switch to from the tray menu at any time.

faqItems.question: Is HTWind open source?
faqItems.answer: Yes. HTWind is published on GitHub under the GPL 3.0 license for personal use, experimentation, and community-driven improvement.

faqItems.question: Are contributions welcome?
faqItems.answer: Yes. You can open issues, share ideas in Discussions, and submit pull requests for widgets, templates, documentation, and core app improvements.
